title: Creating a day-of-the-following-month term lists it after the Net terms
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop creates a new term due on the 10th of the following month.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • All twelve standard terms are active and COD is the default for new customers.
  • A new name {Term-A} that no term has.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-09 Tenth.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Credit Term".
  2. Type {Term-A} in Name.
  3. Click the Day box.
  4. Type 10 in the Day box.
  5. Click "Create Credit Term".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the "New Credit Term" window opens.
  • Step 2: the Name reads {Term-A}.
  • Step 3: "Due day of the following month" is chosen.
  • Step 4: the blue information line shows below the options.
  • Step 5: the toast "{Term-A} created" shows; {Term-A} is listed after Net 120 and before Credit Hold, with Due "10th of the following month" and 0 customers and 0 vendors.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list), story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S3-R7: “On Create, the window closes, a success toast shows "{name} created", and the term appears on the Active tab in its S1-R5 position, with 0 customers and 0 vendors, available at once in every customer and vendor Credit Terms dropdown.”
  • S1-R7, a day of the following month term: “A "day of the following month" term: "{ordinal day} of the following month", for example "10th of the following month", "1st of the following month", "22nd of the following month"”
